sq.ANSWER:
The realloc() is used to reallocate the memory size when the existing is not sufficient. It returns a pointer to the newly allocated memory block on success and a NULL pointer on failure.

Syntax

void * realloc ( void * ptr, size_type size ); Where

          • ptr - Pointer to the original block of memory
          • size-type - data type size
          • size – new size of the memory block in bytes

  • Initially, the memory space of 7 bytes has been allocated for the pointer, str. Later, the memory space for str has been reallocated to 15 bytes.

    PROGRAM:

    #include <stdio.h> #include <stdlib.h> #include <string.h> int main()

    {

    char *str;

    // Allocating memory str = (char *) malloc(7); strcpy(str, "Basic C");

    printf("String : %s - Address : %u\n", str, str);

    // Reallocating memory

    str = (char *) realloc(str, 15); strcat(str, " Program");

    printf("String : %s - Address : %u\n", str, str); free(str); return(0);

    }

    Output

    String : Basic C - Address :65526

    String : Basic C Program - Address :65538

#include <stdio.h> #include <stdlib.h>

// Function to allocate memory for a matrix

int** allocateMatrix(int rows, int cols) {

int** matrix = (int**)malloc(rows * sizeof(int*)); for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {

matrix[i] = (int*)malloc(cols * sizeof(int));

}

return matrix;

}

// Function to input values into a matrix

void inputMatrixValues(int** matrix, int rows, int cols) { for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {

for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {

printf("Enter value for matrix[%d][%d]: ", i, j); scanf("%d", &matrix[i][j]);

}

}

}

// Function to multiply two matrices

int** multiplyMatrices(int** matrixA, int** matrixB, int rowsA, int colsA, int colsB) {

// Allocate memory for the result matrix int** result = allocateMatrix(rowsA, colsB);

 

// Perform matrix multiplication for (int i = 0; i < rowsA; i++) {

for (int j = 0; j < colsB; j++) { result[i][j] = 0;

for (int k = 0; k < colsA; k++) {

result[i][j] += matrixA[i][k] * matrixB[k][j];

}

}

}

return result;

}

// Function to display a matrix

void displayMatrix(int** matrix, int rows, int cols) { printf("Resulting matrix:\n");

for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) { for (int j = 0; j < cols; j++) {

printf("%d ", matrix[i][j]);

}

printf("\n");

}

}

// Function to deallocate memory used for a matrix

void deallocateMatrix(int** matrix, int rows) { for (int i = 0; i < rows; i++) {

free(matrix[i]);

}

free(matrix);

}

 

int main() {

int rowsA, colsA, rowsB, colsB;

// Input dimensions for the matrices

printf("Enter the number of rows for matrix A: "); scanf("%d", &rowsA);

printf("Enter the number of columns for matrix A (and rows for matrix B): "); scanf("%d", &colsA);

printf("Enter the number of columns for matrix B: "); scanf("%d", &colsB);

 

// Ensure matrix multiplication is possible (colsA == rowsB) rowsB = colsA;

 

// Dynamically allocate memory for matrices A and B int** matrixA = allocateMatrix(rowsA, colsA);

int** matrixB = allocateMatrix(rowsB, colsB);

// Input values for matrix A printf("Enter values for matrix A:\n");

inputMatrixValues(matrixA, rowsA, colsA);

// Input values for matrix B printf("Enter values for matrix B:\n");

inputMatrixValues(matrixB, rowsB, colsB);

// Multiply matrices A and B

int** resultMatrix = multiplyMatrices(matrixA, matrixB, rowsA, colsA, colsB);

// Display the resulting matrix displayMatrix(resultMatrix, rowsA, colsB);

// Deallocate memory used for matrices deallocateMatrix(matrixA, rowsA); deallocateMatrix(matrixB, rowsB); deallocateMatrix(resultMatrix, rowsA);

 

return 0;

}

Implement a C program that dynamically allocates memory for two matrices, performs matrix multiplication, and then deallocates the memory. The program should include the following functionalities:

    1. Allocate Memory Dynamically to use dynamic memory allocation to create matrices of the specified dimensions.
    2. Input Matrix Values to provide the values for each matrix.
    3. Perform Matrix Multiplication to compute the product of the two matrix and store the result in a third matrix.
    4. Display the resulting matrix after multiplication.
    5. Deallocate the memory used for matrices to prevent memory leaks.
